q_en: Which word takes someone out of a sentence, and what happens to the word after it?
q_ar: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تُخْرِجُ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْجُمْلَةِ؟ وَمَاذَا يَحْدُثُ لِآخِرِ الْكَلِمَةِ بَعْدَهَا؟
not_yet: Every case of the word after a negative with a named word (two endings are allowed there).
The other exception words (such as khalā and ʿadā) and exception before the group: later study.
Sentences where إِلَّا only means “but” and takes out nothing.
not_yet_ar: كُلُّ حَالَاتِ الْمُسْتَثْنَى بَعْدَ النَّفْيِ مَعَ ذِكْرِ الْمُسْتَثْنَى مِنْهُ (يَجُوزُ فِيهَا وَجْهَانِ).
أَدَوَاتُ الِاسْتِثْنَاءِ الْأُخْرَى (مِثْلُ خَلَا وَعَدَا) وَتَقْدِيمُ الْمُسْتَثْنَى: لِلدِّرَاسَةِ لَاحِقًا.
الْجُمَلُ الَّتِي تَكُونُ فِيهَا إِلَّا بِمَعْنَى «لَكِنْ» وَلَا تُخْرِجُ شَيْئًا.

sents: The students attended the lesson except Salim.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْكُتُبَ غَيْرَ الْكِتَابِ الْكَبِيرِ.
The boy read the books except the big book.
The guests ate the food apart from the bread.

lines: In each sentence: who or what is taken out, and which word takes it out?
فِي كُلِّ جُمْلَةٍ: مَنْ أَوْ مَا الَّذِي أُخْرِجَ؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ أَخْرَجَتْهُ؟
Look at the last letter of the word after إِلَّا in sentences 1 and 4. Is it the same?
اُنْظُرْ إِلَى آخِرِ الْكَلِمَةِ بَعْدَ إِلَّا فِي ١ وَ٤. هَلْ هُوَ وَاحِدٌ؟
In sentence 4, who attended: everyone but one, or only one?
فِي الْجُمْلَةِ ٤: مَنْ حَضَرَ؟ الْجَمِيعُ إِلَّا وَاحِدًا أَمْ وَاحِدٌ وَحْدَهُ؟

slides.head_en: Three ways to take one out

cards.def_en: After a full sentence the one taken out ends in ـَ or ـً.
Nouns that work like إِلَّا. The next word ends in ـِ.

cards.def_ar: الْكَلِمَةُ بَعْدَ إِلَّا تَأْخُذُ حَرَكَةَ عَمَلِهَا
cards.def_en: Nobody is named before it. The word after إِلَّا takes the ending of its own job.

slides.head_en: The system: the ending after إِلَّا, غَيْر and سِوَى
slides.head_ar: النِّظَامُ: آخِرُ الْكَلِمَةِ بَعْدَ أَدَاةِ الِاسْتِثْنَاءِ
rows: fatḥa on غَيْر, kasra on the next
مَا ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَّا إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ
slides.note: In the last row the fatḥa is also found. The word after إِلَّا stands in for the one named before it.
slides.note_ar: فِي الصَّفِّ الْأَخِيرِ يَجُوزُ النَّصْبُ كَذَلِكَ. الْكَلِمَةُ بَعْدَ إِلَّا بَدَلٌ مِنَ الْكَلِمَةِ الْمَذْكُورَةِ قَبْلَهَا.

slides.head_en: “Except” and “only”: the same words, opposite meaning
rows: I read the books but one
slides.note: “Except” takes one out of a group. “Only” leaves one in and sends everyone else out.
slides.note_ar: «إِلَّا» تُخْرِجُ وَاحِدًا مِنَ الْجَمِيعِ. وَ«مَا … إِلَّا» تُبْقِي وَاحِدًا وَتُخْرِجُ الْجَمِيعَ.

slides.head_en: Try: translate, then name the ending
items: The companions came except Umar · عُمَرَ ـَ
Only Umar came · عُمَرُ ـُ (the doer)
The men travelled apart from Ahmad
There is only a book in the room
He went only to the mosque

slides.why: A student writes this. Wrong! After a full sentence the one taken out ends in ـًا: إِلَّا سَالِمًا. (Only in مَا حَضَرَ إِلَّا سَالِمٌ is ـٌ right, because there the word is the one who attended.)
slides.why_ar: كَتَبَ طَالِبٌ هَذِهِ الْجُمْلَةَ. هَذَا خَطَأٌ! بَعْدَ جُمْلَةٍ تَامَّةٍ يَنْتَهِي الْمُسْتَثْنَى بِفَتْحَةٍ: إِلَّا سَالِمًا. أَمَّا فِي «مَا حَضَرَ إِلَّا سَالِمٌ» فَالضَّمَّةُ صَحِيحَةٌ لِأَنَّهُ الْفَاعِلُ.

slides.head_en: Text 1: the water, and the first line of faith
lines: وَالْمَاءُ الْكَثِيرُ لَا يَتَنَجَّسُ إِلَّا إِذَا تَغَيَّرَ طَعْمُهُ أَوْ لَوْنُهُ أَوْ رِيحُهُ
Plentiful water does not become impure unless its taste, colour or smell changes.
وَمَعْنَى لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ : لَا مَعْبُودَ بِحَقٍّ فِي الْوُجُودِ إِلَّا اللهُ
And the meaning of "there is no god but God": no one in existence is worshipped in truth except God.
slides.source: Matn Safīnat al-Najā of Sālim b. Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī

slides.head_en: Text 2: the same rule in verse
lines: Plentiful water is not made impure by the falling of
an impurity into it, unless it changes —
طَعْمٌ لَهُ أَوْ لَوْنٌ أَوْ رِيْحٌ جَلَا
its taste, or colour, or smell, clearly;
but small amounts become impure, without exception.
slides.source: Nayl al-Rajā, the verse form of Safīnat al-Najā (Muḥammad Maʿṣūm al-Sharbūnī)
gloss: the falling (بِاعْتِرَا = by the falling of)

slides.head_en: Text 3: سِوَى and إِلَّا in a counsel text
lines: أَرْكَانُ الْعُمْرَةِ: هِيَ أَرْكَانُ الْحَجِّ إِلَّا الْوُقُوفَ فَلَيْسَ مِنْهَا
The pillars of the ʿumra are the pillars of the pilgrimage, except the standing at ʿArafa, which is not one of them.
فَلَا زَكَاةَ فِيمَا سِوَى النَّعَمِ السَّائِمَةِ
So there is no zakāt on anything other than grazing livestock.
slides.source: al-Risāla al-Jāmiʿa of Imām Aḥmad b. Zayn al-Ḥabashī

lines: إِلَّا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ الصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِالْحَقِّ وَتَوَاصَوْاْ بِالصَّبْرِ
except those who believe, and do righteous deeds, and urge one another to the truth, and urge one another to patience.
إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ
except one who comes to God with a sound heart.

can: I can say which word takes something out of a sentence (إِلَّا, غَيْر, سِوَى) and which word is taken out.
I can give the right ending to the word after إِلَّا: ـَ in a full sentence, and the ending of its own job after مَا … إِلَّا.
I can read مَا … إِلَّا and لَا … إِلَّا as “only”, and إِلَّا إِذَا as “unless”.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَعْرِفَ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تُخْرِجُ شَيْئًا مِنَ الْجُمْلَةِ (إِلَّا وَغَيْرُ وَسِوَى) وَالْكَلِمَةَ الْمُخْرَجَةَ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَضَعَ آخِرَ الْكَلِمَةِ بَعْدَ إِلَّا: فَتْحَةً بَعْدَ جُمْلَةٍ تَامَّةٍ، وَحَرَكَةَ عَمَلِهَا بَعْدَ مَا … إِلَّا.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ «مَا … إِلَّا» وَ«لَا … إِلَّا» بِمَعْنَى الْحَصْرِ، وَ«إِلَّا إِذَا» بِمَعْنَى «إِنْ لَمْ».

options: And plentiful water does not become impure.
Water: plentiful water, and when it becomes impure.
items.answer: Water: plentiful water, and when it becomes impure.
items.model: Water: plentiful water, and when it becomes impure.

items.ar_q: تَرْجِمْ.
options: And plentiful water does not become impure.
Water: plentiful water, and when it becomes impure.
items.answer: And plentiful water does not become impure.
items.model: And plentiful water does not become impure.

items.en: What does إِلَّا إِذَا add? Translate it.
items.ar_q: مَاذَا تُضِيفُ إِلَّا إِذَا؟
items.model: “Unless”: the one case in which the water does become impure.

items.en: Line 1: which three things may change? Write them in Arabic.

items.model: طَعْمُهُ (its taste), لَوْنُهُ (its colour), رِيحُهُ (its smell).

items.en: What does this small word do between the three?

options: No one in existence is worshipped in truth except God.
And plentiful water does not become impure.

items.en: What does the ending ـهُ point to?
items.ar_q: إِلَى مَاذَا تَرْجِعُ ـهُ؟
options: No one in existence is worshipped in truth except God.
And plentiful water does not become impure.
Water: plentiful water, and when it becomes impure.

items.en: True or false? “Plentiful water becomes impure whenever anything falls into it.”
items.ar_q: صَحِيحٌ أَمْ خَطَأٌ؟ «يَتَنَجَّسُ الْمَاءُ الْكَثِيرُ كُلَّمَا وَقَعَ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ».
items.model: False. The text says it does not become impure unless its taste, colour or smell changes.
items.note: The text says it does not become impure unless its taste, colour or smell changes.

items.ar: لَا مَعْبُودَ بِحَقٍّ فِي الْوُجُودِ إِلَّا اللهُ

options: No one in existence is worshipped in truth except God.

items.en: ★ In لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ the last word ends in ـُ, not in ـَ. Why?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا يَنْتَهِي آخِرُ «اللهُ» بِضَمَّةٍ لَا بِفَتْحَةٍ؟
items.model: It stands in place of the word after لَا (“no god”), so it has that word’s ending (ـُ). The ـَ belongs to a full positive sentence.

items.en: ★ In line 1 a whole clause follows إِلَّا (إِذَا تَغَيَّرَ …); in line 2 one word follows it. Which line gives a condition, and which gives one name?
items.ar_q: ★ أَيُّ السَّطْرَيْنِ يُعْطِي شَرْطًا؟ وَأَيُّهُمَا يُعْطِي اسْمًا وَاحِدًا؟
items.model: Line 1 gives a condition (“unless it changes”); line 2 gives one name (God).

sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–112
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
The Habib gave the boy a small book.
ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.
وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.
The boy read the wird in the morning.
ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.
شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.
Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.
